figures.caption: The odometer records accumulated distance. The speedometer records how fast that distance is changing.
Constant velocity gives a horizontal velocity graph and a straight distance graph. The same number  60  appears as a height, a slope, and a rate.
When velocity changes by steps, distance is built from several straight pieces. Each piece has its own slope.
Area above the time axis counts positive. Area below the time axis counts negative. The signed area under the velocity graph is  80-30=50 , matching the change in signed position.
Step velocity gives a piecewise linear position graph. The signed rectangle areas  2+4+1-3+5  equal the net change  9-0 .
As the second point  Q  moves toward  P , the secant lines approach the tangent line. The slope of that tangent line is the instantaneous velocity.
For an increasing velocity  v(t)=t^2 , left rectangles underestimate the area and right rectangles overestimate it. More rectangles make both estimates better.

The main ideas of the book are connected from the beginning. The derivative measures local change. The integral accumulates change. Approximation makes both useful. Differential equations express laws in the language of change.
Each rectangle gives one signed change in position. Rectangles above the axis count positive; rectangles below the axis count negative.
Two different velocity histories can have the same displacement. Signed area gives the net change but does not determine the velocity at each time.
The real line turns numbers into points and distances.
Open circles mean endpoints are excluded. Filled circles mean endpoints are included.
The inequality  |x-a|<\varepsilon  means that  x  lies within distance  \varepsilon  of  a .
The diagonal of a unit square has length  \sqrt2 , the number whose square is  2 .
Nested intervals trap one number. For the real line, that trapped point exists. For the rational numbers alone, this example traps a missing point.
A function assigns an output to each input in its domain.
The full circle gives two  y -values for many  x -values. The upper semicircle gives exactly one.
A piecewise function can describe motion whose rule changes.
The difference quotient is the slope of the secant line through the points with inputs  a  and  a+h .
Adding outside the function shifts vertically. Changing the input inside the function shifts horizontally.
The square function is even. The cube function is odd.
Zeros divide the  x -axis into intervals. On each interval, the graph is either above or below the axis until it crosses again.
In  f(g(x)) , the function  g  acts first. Its output becomes the input of  f .
The square function is not one-to-one on all real numbers. On the restricted domain  [0,\infty) , it has inverse  \sqrt{x} .
The average cost approaches the variable cost per item as the fixed cost is spread over more items.
On the unit circle, cosine and sine are coordinates of the point reached by angle  \theta .
Exponential and logarithm functions are inverses, so their graphs reflect across the line  y=x .
Linear growth adds equal amounts. Exponential growth multiplies by equal factors.
A sinusoidal model records a repeating motion by its midline, amplitude, and period.
The small window is not false; it is incomplete. A wider window reveals behavior the first picture cannot show.
A finite sample can miss oscillation. The left picture suggests  f(x)=0 . The right picture shows the hidden motion.
Zeros divide the  x -axis into intervals where the function has a fixed sign.
The coffee cools toward room temperature. A good model should respect that long-term behavior.
The slopes of the secant lines approach the slope of the tangent line at  t=2 .
The limit watches nearby values.  It does not have to equal the value of the function at the point.
A two-sided limit exists only when nearby values approach one common target.
For  x\neq1 ,  \dfrac{x^2-1}{x-1}=x+1 .  The limit sees the nearby line, not the missing point.
The oscillating graph is trapped between  y=-x^2  and  y=x^2 .  The walls close in at  0 .
The left and right sides approach different values.  Therefore the two-sided limit does not exist.
The graph of  1/(x-2)  falls without bound from the left and rises without bound from the right.
The graph of  \dfrac{x^2+1}{x-1}  has a vertical asymptote  x=1  and a slant asymptote  y=x+1 .
For  \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L , every horizontal band around  L  must contain the graph over some punctured vertical strip around  a .
The function  \dfrac{x^2-1}{x-1}  has the graph of  y=x+1 , except for a missing point at  x=1 .
Nearby,  (F(x))^2  follows  y=(2x+1)^2  and approaches  9 .  At  x=1  the value is  1 .  The composition has a limit, but it is not continuous at  1 .
Two failures: the outer function is not continuous at  L , or the inner function has no two-sided limit.
Three common ways continuity can fail: a hole, a jump, or a vertical asymptote.
A continuous graph that goes from negative to positive must cross the  x -axis.
Without continuity, a graph can jump over an intermediate value.
A continuous function on a closed finite interval reaches its highest and lowest values.
A jump creates two different one-sided limits, so the two-sided limit fails.
The values of  1/x^2  grow without bound near  0 .  This is infinite behavior, not a finite limit.
Without continuity, a function can jump over an intermediate value.
On  (0,1) , the function  f(x)=x  approaches its lowest and highest possible values but never reaches them.
The sequence  1/n  settles toward  0 .  The sequence  (-1)^n  keeps jumping between two values.
The sequence  a_n=1-1/n  increases toward  1  without passing it.
Limits are the center.  Continuity, asymptotes, sequences, and tangent slopes all use the same idea of controlled approach.
Graph for reading one-sided limits, function values, and discontinuities.
The average rate of change is the slope of the secant line through two graph points.
Average rates from data are secant slopes between measured points.
Secant slopes approach the tangent slope as the second point approaches the first.
A tangent line can cross the curve.  Tangency is about limiting slope, not merely touching.
At a corner, the left and right limiting slopes can disagree.  Then the derivative does not exist.
The graph of  f  shows height.  The graph of  f'  shows tangent slope.
The derivative graph records the slopes of the original graph.
Near  x=4 , the tangent line gives a simple model for  \sqrt{x} .
The differential  dy  is the tangent-line change.  The actual change is  \Delta y .
The graph of  y=|x|  is continuous at  0 , but the two limiting slopes disagree.
Differentiability can fail in different ways.  Continuity rules out jumps, but not corners, cusps, or vertical tangents.
The derivative formula gives the tangent slope without returning to the limit definition.
Position, velocity, and acceleration are linked by derivatives.  The position has a maximum when the velocity changes sign from positive to negative.
The particle returns to its starting position, so its displacement is  0 , but it has traveled a total distance of  8 .
At the highest point, the velocity is  0 , but the acceleration is still  -32\text{ ft/s}^2 .
The function  s(t)=|t|  is continuous at  0 , but it has no derivative there.
A finite plot can miss a nondifferentiable point if it is not sampled.
The derivative is one idea with several connected meanings.
Noisy position data still suggest a smooth motion, but slopes estimated from nearby points can vary.
When both factors change, a product changes by two main strips and a small corner.
A chain diagram records the order in which the function is built.
Implicit differentiation gives the tangent slope without solving the circle into upper and lower functions.
For  0<h<\pi/2 , the small triangle lies inside the sector, which lies inside the larger triangle.
The derivative of the sine curve is the cosine curve.
For simple harmonic motion, acceleration is proportional to displacement and points in the opposite direction.
The base  e  is chosen so that  e^x  has slope  1  at  x=0 .
Inverse functions are reflections across  y=x .  Corresponding tangent slopes are reciprocals.
The horizontal tangent to  y=x^3  reflects into a vertical tangent to  y=\sqrt[3]{x} .
The graph of  y=\arcsin x  is the reflection of the restricted sine graph across  y=x .
The function  \cosh x  is even, while  \sinh x  is odd.
The parametrization  X=\cosh t ,  Y=\sinh t  lies on the hyperbola  X^2-Y^2=1 .
The three basic inverse branches. The branch of  \operatorname{arcosh}  begins at  (1,0) ;  \operatorname{artanh}  has vertical asymptotes at  x=\pm1 .
Near the lowest point, a catenary resembles a parabola.  Farther away, the hyperbolic cosine shape rises differently.
A changing product has two first-order contributions, not one.
The same two functions in different orders produce different chains.
A good derivative calculation reads the function first and checks the result afterward.
The derivative gives information about the shape of the original graph.
The sign of velocity tells whether the position is increasing or decreasing.
The derivative sign chart predicts the rise and fall of the original graph.
For  g(x)=|x| , the derivative is undefined at  0 .  So  0  is a critical number.
A local maximum may not be the absolute maximum.  Endpoints must be checked.
For  f(x)=x^2  on  [1,3] , the secant slope is  4 .  The tangent slope at  x=2  is also  4 .
Rolle’s Theorem says that equal endpoint heights force at least one horizontal tangent inside.
Both positions increase on the interval, but one bends upward and the other bends downward.
Concave up means slopes increase.  Concave down means slopes decrease.
The sign of  f''  gives the concavity of  f .
The first derivative locates turning behavior.  The second derivative locates bending behavior.
A calculus sketch combines asymptotes, first derivative signs, and second derivative signs.
An endpoint can be highest or lowest simply because the interval stops.
Without continuity, the endpoint secant slope may not appear as any tangent slope.
A corner can create a turn without any horizontal tangent.
When  f'(0)=0  and  f''(0)=0 , the second derivative test is silent.
A first derivative sign chart gives turning behavior.  A second derivative sign chart gives bending behavior.
The ladder length is fixed, so  x^2+y^2=100 .  The changing lengths  x  and  y  have related rates.
Similar triangles relate the person’s position  x , the shadow length  s , and the tip position  p=x+s .
Similar triangles give  r/h=4/12 , so the cone volume can be written using  h  alone.
The river supplies one side, so the fencing constraint is  2x+y=200 .
Cutting out four squares of side length  x  leaves an open box with volume  V=x(12-2x)^2 .
For a closed cylinder with fixed volume, the surface area is minimized when height equals diameter.
The total path length is  D(x)=\sqrt{x^2+a^2}+\sqrt{(L-x)^2+b^2} .
Near  x=25 , the tangent line to  y=\sqrt{x}  gives a quick estimate of  \sqrt{x} .
For a sphere,  dV=4\pi r^2\,dr : surface area times a small change in radius.
The model  H=100\tan\theta  becomes very sensitive when  \theta  is large.
Newton’s method replaces the curve by its tangent line and uses the tangent’s  x -intercept as the next guess.
For  f(x)=x^3-2x+2 , Newton’s method starting at  0  cycles between  0  and  1 .
The equation  y'=ky  gives exponential growth when  k>0  and exponential decay when  k<0 .
Newton’s law of cooling says the temperature difference  T-T_s  decays exponentially.
For the logistic equation,  P'  is positive below  K  and negative above  K .  The carrying capacity  K  is stable.
Logistic solutions move toward the carrying capacity  K .  From below they rise toward  K ; from above they fall toward  K .
Reflecting  B  across the mirror turns the broken reflected path into a straight path from  A  to  B^* .
When speed changes at a boundary, the least-time path usually bends.
The critical point  q=40  maximizes the formula on a larger domain, but it is not an allowed production level.
A local high point can lose to an endpoint or to another part of the graph.
The tangent line at  x_0=1  crosses the axis at the root  -2 , not at the intended root  2 .
The chapter’s methods all follow the same modeling path: translate, differentiate, solve, and interpret.
A more realistic container model can assign different costs to the side wall and the two circular ends.
Newton’s law of cooling models the excess temperature  T-22  as exponential decay.
For constant velocity, displacement is the area of a rectangle under the velocity graph.
For piecewise constant velocity, displacement is a sum of rectangle areas.
A sampled velocity table leads naturally to rectangular distance estimates.
Area above the time axis counts positive.  Area below the time axis counts negative for displacement.
Left endpoint rectangles estimate the area under  y=x^2  on  [0,2] .
For an increasing function, left rectangles give a lower sum and right rectangles give an upper sum.
For  y=x  on  [0,2] , rectangular sums approach the known triangle area  2 .
A partition divides the interval. A sample point in each subinterval determines the rectangle height.
The exact area under  y=x^2  on  [0,2]  is the limit of these rectangular sums:  \int_0^2 x^2\,dx=8/3 .
The integral counts area below the axis negatively and area above the axis positively.
The signed rectangle areas are  2 ,  -2 , and  3 .  Their sum is the displacement.
Accumulation over  [a,b]  is the sum of accumulation over  [a,c]  and  [c,b] .
The average value is the constant height that gives the same accumulated area.
For an odd function on a symmetric interval, the two signed areas cancel.
For an increasing function, left endpoint rectangles give lower sums and right endpoint rectangles give upper sums.  As the widths shrink, the two sums squeeze together.
A finite jump does not prevent integrability.  The jump occurs at one point, and one point has no width.
This picture can only hint at the function  D .  In every interval, the graph has points at height  1  and points at height  0 .
Energy use is accumulated power.  The area under the power graph has units of kilowatt-hours.
When the endpoint moves from  x  to  x+h , the accumulation changes by the area of a thin strip.
As the right endpoint  x  moves, the accumulated area  A(x)  changes.
The change in an accumulation function is the thin strip from  x  to  x+h .
A jump in  f  can produce a corner in the accumulation function  A .
Continuity squeezes the average height of a thin strip toward  f(x) .
The integral of  2x+3  from  1  to  4  is the area of a trapezoid.
Signed velocity gives displacement.  Total distance requires adding the absolute changes.
Antiderivatives of the same function differ by vertical shifts.  Their slopes at the same  x -value are equal.
The same interval with opposite orientations gives integrals with opposite signs.
The substitution  x=u^2  stretches the measuring scale.  Equal  u -steps do not give equal  x -steps.
A jump discontinuity in  f  can produce a corner in the accumulation function  A .
The integral of  x  from  -1  to  1  is zero because positive and negative signed areas cancel.
The Fundamental Theorem connects rate, accumulation, antiderivative, and net change.
To reconstruct  Q(t) , accumulate the measured rate  R(t) .
A vertical strip has height  2x-x^2 , so the area is  \int_0^2(2x-x^2)\,dx .
A horizontal strip has length  (2-y^2)-y^2 , so we integrate with respect to  y .
Volume by slicing: a differential slice of thickness  \Delta x  has volume approximately  A(x)\Delta x .
Rotating the region under  y=\sqrt{x}  around the  x -axis gives disk slices.
Rotating around the  y -axis suggests horizontal slices and an integral in  y .
A vertical strip rotated around the  y -axis makes a cylindrical shell.
The shell height is  1/x , so  x\cdot(1/x)=1 .  The shell setup is especially simple.
For  \lambda(x)=2+x  on  [0,4] , more mass lies to the right, so the center of mass is right of the midpoint.
A triangular lamina can be handled by vertical slices.  Each slice contributes mass and moment.
Work is the accumulated area under a force-versus-position graph.
The farther the spring is stretched, the larger the force needed to hold it.
A piece  y  units below the roof must be lifted  y  units.
Each water slice has the same area, but the lower slices must be lifted farther.
A horizontal strip has nearly constant pressure because its depth is nearly constant.
For the triangular plate, the strip width is a linear function of depth.
For a symmetric vertical window, the centroid depth gives the total force quickly.
The average value is the height of a rectangle with the same area as the region under the graph.
For the density  p(x)=2x , probability is area under the density curve.
For a normal density, probabilities are areas under the bell-shaped curve.
A smooth curve is approximated by short straight pieces.  Each small length comes from the Pythagorean theorem.
A small arc segment rotated around the  x -axis sweeps out a thin band.
Rotating the upper semicircle around the  x -axis produces a sphere.
Even a simple curve can lead to a length integral with no elementary antiderivative.
The same region can produce different integrals depending on what quantity is being measured.

The three substitutions are right-triangle substitutions.  The triangles shown assume  x>0  (and  x>a  in the secant case); their side lengths must be nonnegative. For negative  x , use the signed substitution equations and the chosen angle range.
A practical order of questions.  The arrows are not laws; they are a way to begin thinking.
Both curves approach  0 , but the tail of  1/x  has infinite area while the tail of  1/x^2  has finite area.
A function may become infinite near an endpoint and still have finite area.  The rate of blowup matters.
The signed lobes of  \sin x/x  cancel in the improper integral. Replacing the integrand by its absolute value turns every lobe upward and gives infinite area.
The positive and negative pieces of  1/x  cancel symmetrically, but each piece has infinite size.
The expression  \sqrt{x^2-4}  has two real branches of the domain.  A trigonometric substitution must respect the branch.
A practical order of questions for integration.  The order is flexible, but the first step is always to read the integrand.
The area  \int_0^1 e^{-x^2}\,dx  exists, even though the antiderivative is not elementary.
The midpoint rule uses one rectangle whose height is taken at the midpoint.
The trapezoidal rule replaces the graph by the secant line over the interval.
The composite midpoint rule adds midpoint rectangles over smaller subintervals.
For concave-up graphs, trapezoids lie above the curve.  For concave-down graphs, trapezoids lie below.
Simpson’s Rule replaces the graph on two subintervals by the parabola through three sample points.
Forward, backward, and centered differences approximate the tangent slope using nearby secant slopes.
For  f(x)=|x| , the centered difference at  0  equals  0 , but the derivative at  0  does not exist.
At a double root, the graph is tangent to the  x -axis.  Newton’s method still moves toward the root, but much more slowly.

The Newton map  N(x)=(x-1/x)/2  for  f(x)=x^2+1  has a vertical asymptote at zero. The input  1  maps to zero, where the next step is undefined. The nearby input  1.01  maps to about  0.0099505 , whose next image is about  -50.2438 , far below the displayed window.
For a probability density, area under the curve is probability.
High-order numerical rules are most powerful when the function is smooth enough for their error theory.
The equation  y'=1-y  gives a family of solution curves.  An initial condition selects one curve.
A direction field draws the slope prescribed by  y'=1-y  at many points.  Solution curves follow the field.
For  y'=y(1-y) , the arrows show whether solutions move up or down.
Euler’s method follows the slope field by taking one tangent-line step at a time.
Newton’s law of cooling gives exponential approach to the surrounding temperature.
Logistic solutions move toward the carrying capacity.  From below they rise toward  K ; from above they fall toward  K .
The logistic phase line shows how the equation pushes solutions along the  P -axis.
In a threshold model, the population must start above  A  to move toward the carrying capacity  K .
A constant harvest is sustainable only if the harvest line meets the natural growth curve.
With a constant incoming concentration, the salt amount approaches an equilibrium.
Simple harmonic motion oscillates around the equilibrium  y=0 .
Damping multiplies the oscillation by a decaying envelope.
In the undamped model  y''+\omega^2y=A\cos(\gamma t) , the response grows large as  \gamma  approaches  \omega .

A predator-prey system is read in the phase plane.  The point  (R(t),W(t))  moves according to the vector  (R',W') . The plotted orbit is a numerical trajectory from  (80,20) . Its asymmetric shape comes from the stated equations.
The simple oscillator becomes a first-order system in the position-velocity plane.
The separated family  y=1/(C-t)  misses the equilibrium solution  y=0 .
With a large step, Euler’s method can invent behavior opposite to the true solution.
The equation  y'=1-y  gives a family.  The initial condition selects one solution.
The parameter  t  tells how the point moves around the circle.
The equations  x=1+3t,\;y=-2+t  trace a line segment with a direction.
The sideways parabola is easy to trace parametrically:  x=t^2-1,\;y=t .
For  x=t^2-1,\;y=t , the slope is  \dfrac{1}{2t}  when  t\neq0 .
On the unit circle,  y'=0  gives horizontal tangents and  x'=0  gives vertical tangents.
The equations  x=80t,\;y=5+60t-16t^2  give the path and the motion along it.
The circle is traced at constant speed  R , so its length is  2\pi R .
The sphere is built from rotating small arc segments of the upper semicircle.
The counterclockwise parametrization of an ellipse gives the area  \pi ab .
A point on a rolling wheel traces a cycloid.  The picture is scaled by  R .
Polar coordinates describe a point by distance from the origin and angle from the positive  x -axis.
A constant radius gives a circle.  A radius growing with angle gives a spiral.
The polar equation  r=2\cos\theta  is the circle  (x-1)^2+y^2=1 .
Rose curves and limacons are simple in polar coordinates but awkward in Cartesian coordinates.
When  r=1+2\cos\theta , negative values of  r  create an inner loop.
A polar graph is a parametric curve with  \theta  as the parameter.
The polar slope formula gives a horizontal tangent at the top of the circle  r=2\cos\theta .
A small angular slice is approximately a sector of area  \frac12r^2\Delta\theta .
The cardioid area is found by accumulating small sectors.
The two circles intersect at  (1,1)  and at the origin.  The origin is reached at different polar angles.
A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix.
Ellipses close up because  0\le e<1 .  Hyperbolas open because  e>1 .
The polar equation  r=\frac{4}{1+\cos\theta}  is a parabola with focus at the pole.
In polar form, changing  e  changes the conic type.  The focus is at the pole.
In the polar form of an ellipse, the focus is placed at the pole.  The center is not at the pole.
The complex number  a+bi  is the point  (a,b)  in the plane.
Multiplication by  i  rotates the plane by  90^\circ  counterclockwise.
Sine and cosine are projections of circular motion.  Euler’s formula writes that motion as  e^{i\omega t} .
The parametrization  x=t^3,\;y=t^6  pauses at the origin, but the geometric curve is the smooth parabola  y=x^2 .
Using  0\le\theta\le2\pi  for  r=2\cos\theta  traces the same circle twice.
At  t=0 , all three parametrizations have  x'(0)=y'(0)=0 , but their tangents are different.
A cycloid animation should show the rolling circle and the point  P(t)  tracing the curve.
The sequence  c_n=1-\frac1n  approaches  1  from below.
The recursion  a_{n+1}=(a_n+3)/2  moves halfway to  3  at each step.
The partial sums  S_n=\frac12+\frac14+\cdots+\frac1{2^n}  approach  1 .
Grouping the harmonic series into doubled blocks shows that the partial sums keep gaining at least  1/2 .
For a positive decreasing function, rectangle sums and improper integrals control each other.
The alternating harmonic partial sums bounce above and below their limiting value.
The Riemann rearrangement idea: alternate above and below a target, with shrinking overshoots.
Vertical moves to  y=\cos x  followed by horizontal moves to  y=x  produce the contraction iteration. The steps alternate around the fixed point.
A power series has a center  a  and a radius of convergence  R .  Endpoint behavior is not decided by the radius alone.
Inside a smaller interval  [a-r,a+r] , a power series is controlled uniformly by geometric bounds.
Partial sums of the geometric series approach  \frac1{1-x}  on  (-1,1) .
Taylor polynomials for  e^x  match more derivatives at the center  0 .
The remainder is the vertical gap between the function and its Taylor polynomial at the chosen input.
Taylor polynomials for  \sin x  are best near the center  0 , then improve outward as more terms are added.
On  [0,1] , a Taylor polynomial gives a close approximation to  e^{-x^2} , and integrating the polynomial gives an approximation to the area.
The functions  x^n  converge pointwise on  [0,1] , but the convergence is slow near  x=1 .
The spikes for  n=4  and  n=8  become narrower and taller, while each has area  1 .
The function  e^{-1/x^2} , with  f(0)=0 , is positive away from  0  but is infinitely flat at  0 .
The Maclaurin series for  \frac1{1-x}  has radius  1 .  It cannot pass the singularity at  x=1 , even though the function is defined again at  x=2 .
The Taylor series hint that  e^{i\theta}  traces the unit circle.
The complex number  3+4i  is drawn as the point  (3,4)  in the complex plane.
Polar form records a complex number by its length  r  and angle  \theta .
Multiplication by  i  rotates a complex number counterclockwise by  90^\circ .
The equation  z^4=1  has four solutions on the unit circle.
The position  e^{it}  lies on the unit circle.  Its velocity  ie^{it}  is a quarter-turn of the position.
A spring pulls back toward equilibrium.  Newton’s law turns this restoring force into a second-order equation.
The solution of  y''+9y=0  is periodic.  Its amplitude is determined by the initial position and velocity.
For an undamped oscillator, the phase point  (y,y')  moves clockwise around a closed energy curve. Here  \omega=2  and  R=3 ; equal coordinate scales show the ellipse’s two-to-one axis ratio.
A lightly damped oscillator still oscillates, but its amplitude shrinks exponentially.
With damping, resonance produces a large response near the natural frequency, but the amplitude remains finite.
Adding a few sine and cosine waves already creates a more complicated periodic shape.
The product  \sin t\sin(2t)  has signed area zero over  [-\pi,\pi] .
Fourier partial sums approximate a square wave by adding sine waves.  Near each jump, ripples remain.
The boundary of an oriented interval is its ending point minus its starting point.
Splitting an interval creates an artificial boundary at  c , but the two signs at  c  cancel.
In one dimension, an interval has two boundary points.  Flux through those boundary points changes what is inside.
When  q  increases with  x , the outgoing flux from a small interval exceeds the incoming flux.
To optimize a path, we compare it with nearby paths that keep the endpoints fixed.
The brachistochrone is not the shortest path.  It is the path of shortest time.
Calculus is one connected language: change, accumulation, approximation, models, and boundary terms.
Three solutions of  y'=2\sqrt{|y|}  pass through  (0,0) : immediate departure, departure after time one, and the zero solution.
Completing the square reveals the vertex and the minimum value.
Absolute value inequalities are distance statements.
Slope measures vertical change per horizontal change.
The intercepts are often the quickest way to sketch a line in general form.
The circle  (x-2)^2+(y+3)^2=25  has center  (2,-3)  and radius  5 .
Vertex form shows the shift and stretch immediately.
The ellipse  \frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1  has semi-axis lengths  3  and  2 .
A hyperbola approaches its asymptotes but does not cross them far from the center.
The distance formula is the Pythagorean Theorem.
Replacing  x  by  x-3  shifts right  3 ; subtracting  1  shifts down  1 .
The starting point of the square-root graph moves from  (0,0)  to  (2,1) .
On the unit circle, radian measure equals arc length.
The cosine is the  x -coordinate and the sine is the  y -coordinate on the unit circle.
Sine and cosine are periodic because the unit circle repeats after a full turn.
The inverse sine reverses the restricted sine function on  [-\pi/2,\pi/2] .
The set of rational numbers with  x^2<2  points toward  \sqrt2 , which is missing from  \mathbb Q .
An increasing sequence trapped below an upper bound must approach its least upper bound.
Shrinking nested closed intervals trap a single real number.
A continuous graph that goes from negative to positive must cross the  x -axis.
A jump discontinuity can change sign without crossing  0 .
Continuity on a closed interval forces the supremum of the values to be reached.
The function  1/x  is continuous on  (0,1) , but no single input tolerance works everywhere.
The viewing window can reveal or conceal features of the same function.
A plotted line may hide the fact that the original formula is undefined at  x=1 .
Sampling too few points can give a misleading picture of a rapidly changing function.
Taylor polynomials approximate  \sin x  best near their center  0 .
